decisions.reason: The candidate already requires controlled high-speed splashing and already permits whisk-position, bowl, or guard mitigation; the source adds no necessary state change.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records that the bowls must lift out without obstruction from the whisk or motor assembly.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records fast, preferably tool-free whisk removal for cleaning and event part swapping.
The source references the previously selected higher RPM range but does not change the motor speed range, controls, or intended speed modes.
Bowl geometry is mentioned only as a possible splash-control method; no concrete bowl size, depth, capacity, or geometry change is selected.
The reference to the more powerful motor does not alter prolonged-use expectations or the existing maximum-speed duty constraint.
Keeping the machine clean while mixing concerns splash control and does not modify the dispensing-path seal or leak-prevention requirement.
The source addresses whisk positioning and splash control during mixing, not the dispensing mechanism, sequence, flow, or drip behavior.
The source states product usability constraints but does not change the BOM deliverable or select a different component for it.
The cleaning references concern removable bowls and whisks; they do not change the spout or dispensing-path cleaning requirement.
Refining the layout and considering a discreet guard does not necessarily change the established enclosure dimensions or form-factor constraint.
The source contains no decision affecting placard text, position, or customer-facing orientation.
